title: GPU stack compatibility sleuthing notes
content:
Context:
- Intermittent OOMs seen while running a long autoregressive generation (seq_len ~ 8192) on dedicated test node (g5.12xlarge-like). Happens ~30–60m into a continuous load test.
- Suspect: driver/libcuda mismatch, or mixing of system CUDA toolkit + container runtime libs. Also looking at kernel driver updates (node had a driver update during early Feb maintenance window).

Environment snapshot (collected 2025-02-28T09:12):
- kernel: 6.4.17-arch-custom
- nvidia-driver: 535.54.03 (from nvidia-installer)
- CUDA toolkit install: /usr/local/cuda-12.2 (symlinked /usr/local/cuda -> cuda-12.2)
- container base image: ubuntu:22.04 + nvidia/cuda:12.1-runtime inside Docker
- container runtime: Docker 24.0 + nvidia-container-toolkit 1.15
- python packages: torch 2.2.0+cu121 wheel built with 12.1, tritonlib 2.0.5, accelerate 0.21

Symptoms (notes):
- Process killed with no Python-level exception; dmesg shows GPU OOM and driver messages.
- Occurs under mixed-precision (amp) in most runs, but reproducible under fp32 if seq_len increased.
- Sometimes the container restarts and subsequent runs succeed for a few hours, then fail again.

Commands tried and outputs (timeline):
1) Basic sanity
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,cuda_version --format=csv
  -> driver_version: 535.54.03, cuda_version: 12.2
- inside container: python -c "import ctypes, sys; print('libcuda', ctypes.CDLL('libcuda.so.1'))"
  -> loads libcuda from host libs (path resolves), but runtime version mismatch suspected.

2) Check for duplicate libcuda / libcudart
- find /usr -name 'libcuda*.so*' -o -name 'libcudart*.so*' | sed -e 's/^/  /'
  -> multiple entries: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 (host), /usr/local/cuda-12.2/lib64/libcudart.so.12.2 (toolkit), container image has /usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64/libcudart.so.12.1

3) Run reproducer under strace-like wrapper to capture dlopen paths
- PYTHONVERBOSE=2 python generate_long_sequence.py 2>&1 | tee dlopen.log
  -> observed: dlopen("/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1") by libtorch, but later UNABLE to find certain symbol versions in libcudart from container.

4) Attempt LD_PRELOAD trick (temporary test)
- LD_PRELOAD=/usr/local/cuda-12.2/lib64/libcudart.so.12.2 python generate_long_sequence.py
  -> short-term improvement: run survived longer (~90m) but still OOMs eventually. Suspect not pure symbol mismatch.

5) Recreate with driver pinned to older version (lab node)
- Rolled back to driver 525.116.04 (matching image used in earlier golden runs)
- After rollback, same workload ran ~8h without OOMs.
  -> Strong indicator driver ABI change introduced instability under heavy KV cache churn.

6) Re-upgrade to 535 and instrumented kernel logs:
- dmesg excerpt (when failure occurred):
  [  605.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 79, pid=12822, 0 GPU has fallen off the bus.
  [  605.123459] NVRM: RmInitAdapter failed! (0x36:0x46:124)
  [  605.123461] NVRM: rm init failed, device minor number 0
- Kernel rebind/recovery triggered; container processes killed.

Error snippets captured from worker logs:
- "NCCL WARN TensorPeerAccess: cannot map peer memory"
- Torch CUDA OOM sequence:
  RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.00 GiB (GPU 0; total 40.00 GiB; free 1.87 GiB)
  Note: free numbers sometimes lie just prior to crash.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Driver ABI regression (535.x) combined with our long-lived persistent CUDA contexts + aggressive KV cache reuse results in driver-side memory accounting corruption leading to OOMs and device reset. Evidence: rollback to 525 removes issue.
2) Mixed-set of libcudart/libcuda across host and container causing some allocations to be made against different allocators; LD_PRELOAD mitigates slightly but isn't full fix.
3) Kernel module / iommu or PCIe link flakiness causing transient device disconnects under sustained DMA; driver version 535 shows "has fallen off the bus" messages.
4) Application-level leak in kv-cache handling (less likely because same binary + workload on other nodes with 525 is stable).

Quick experiments to run next (notes for follow-ups):
- Reproduce on a clean node with 535 + container using full cuda 12.2 runtime image (avoid mixing 12.1 host container). If still fails, file upstream bug with NVIDIA.
- Try latest 536 nightly driver (if available) to see whether bug fixed.
- Run with NVFUSER/Triton disabled to rule out JIT-ed kernel leak.
- Force explicit cudaDeviceReset() in between runs to see if that prevents accumulation (temporary workaround).
- Add extra checks in our runtime to call cuMemGetInfo() periodically and dump allocator states before reset.

Permanent mitigations considered:
- Pin driver to 525.x across golden fleet until upstream confirms fix.
- Align container base images and host toolkit to exact same CUDA minor versions (12.1 vs 12.2 mismatch is potential footgun).
- Add automated daily smokes that run long seq_len tests to detect regressions early in CI for dedicated images.

Useful commands / snippets (copied for convenience):
- List driver + toolkit files:
  dpkg -l | egrep 'nvidia|cuda' || rpm -qa | egrep 'nvidia|cuda'
- Inspect loaded modules and versions:
  modinfo nvidia | egrep 'version|alias'
- Compare lib symbols quickly:
  readelf -s /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 | egrep 'cuMem|cuCtx' | head -n 20
- Check container ld paths:
  docker run --rm --gpus all --entrypoint sh myimage -c "ldd /usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/torch/lib/libtorch_cuda.so"

Notes to self (less formal):
- When filing the bug, include dmesg, nvidia-smi -q (before crash), container's ldconfig -p, and strace/dlopen log.
- Jon saw similar "fallen off the bus" on a different instance in SEA region — talk to him about fleet timing and kernel upgrades.
- Keep a small golden node with 525 pinned for reproducible baseline.

Open questions:
- Did any kernel module backports occur between 525 and 535 that change DMA mapping behavior?
- Is our custom mempool/kv-cache using undocumented driver features?
- Can we instrument the driver-level bookkeeping by enabling debug log level on effected nodes?

Status: currently running a 24h run on a fresh node with 535 + full CUDA 12.2 runtime to isolate toolkit vs driver mismatch. Will update this doc with outcome.

-- Maya
